introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: Curated knowledge bases such as OMIM are built by experts who read papers and record, entry by entry, what each paper showed; language models can now read those papers, and many system designs (long-context reading, extraction into graphs or tables, agents, draft-then-verify, prompt optimisation) have been proposed for turning documents into structured, cited text, but they were evaluated on different tasks, models, retrieval stacks and scoring, so their results cannot be compared.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: There is no controlled evaluation in which the cited sources, the model, the mechanical guards and the scoring are held fixed and only the generation strategy varies, scored against curator-written per-paper text and structured fields. Scoped to what the log evaluates: one model family, 100 small OMIM phenotype entries (2-12 references) given the curators' own reference list, open-access text only; questions are (1) how much the strategy matters, (2) whether the strategy or what it could read limits agreement with curators, and (3) what a claim-level audit against the cited source can and cannot catch. No claim of generality across models, of clinical use, or of human validation.
search_directions: Real-world burden and bottleneck of manual literature curation for genetic and rare-disease knowledge bases (OMIM, ClinVar, HPO, ClinGen), e.g. growth of the literature, curation backlog and the role of these resources in diagnosis
Surveys and systematic reviews of large language models for literature review, evidence synthesis, systematic-review automation and biomedical knowledge extraction
Foundational papers on retrieval-augmented and long-context generation with citations and on atomic-claim factuality evaluation of long-form generated text
Foundational work on language-model agents and pipelines that write Wikipedia-like or encyclopedic articles from retrieved scientific literature
Open-access availability of the biomedical literature (full text vs abstract only) and its consequences for text mining and machine reading

related_work_strategy.overview: Organise by the paper's own axes (notes.md): (1) literature-to-knowledge-base curation in genetics and biology; (2) intermediate representation versus long-context reading; (3) memory, verification and contamination; (4) supervision by prompt optimisation. Close the section with one paragraph on evaluation: atomic-claim checking, citation support and the validity of model judges (the canonical papers for that paragraph are requested as citation hints in Method 3.3, which the writer should reuse here). Throughout, state the difference from the closest prior work: FlyAOC (memorisation, pipeline and agent harnesses scored against FlyBase curators), GEN-KnowRD (generated rare-disease profiles compared with curated reports), WikiCrow (gene articles against Wikipedia) and Groza et al. 2026 (model memory of rare-disease genes and phenotypes): here the cited papers are fixed, the reference is curators' own text and structured fields, and the generation strategy is the only variable. Do not frame other systems as competitors that were beaten; published systems were not run (log Sec. 12).

content_bullets: One paragraph. Problem: designs for turning papers into structured, cited knowledge-base text are not comparable (idea.md 'Problem').

Benchmark: 100 OMIM phenotype entries, each written from exactly the papers its curators cited, causal gene withheld; one model; shared guards, claim-level audit and scoring; strategies framed as three paradigms, a control and add-ons each tested against its parent (log Sec. 1.3) - never 'nine strategies'.
Primary endpoint named once with required wording: coverage of facts in curator-written per-paper text (do not say 'the OMIM entry').

Results: reading strategies are close at current open access (direct reading 49.1%, evidence graph 48.6%, agentic curator 48.4%, case table first 47.2%; log Sec. 2.2); memory-based strategies far lower (15.1%, 14.6%).

Lead the access claim with the within-paper experiment: hiding full text of the same papers drops coverage from 78.6% to 35.5%, second-hand passages recover to 41.4% (log Sec. 6.2); differences between strategies grow where more full text is readable (log Sec. 2.9).

Audit: removes unsupported claims and flagged all 60 planted single-fact errors, but checks fidelity, not correctness, and passes claims supported only by a later paper's description (log Sec. 11, 6.2).
One clause on scope: one model family, no human validation, open-access text only.

Formalise as in idea.md 'Formal setup': entry e = (h, R), R = {d_1,...,d_n}, access level a(d) in {full text, abstract, title}; strategy S maps (h, R) to draft D (paragraphs citing non-empty subsets of R, genes, inheritance modes, ontology terms, variants).
Input: entry number, title and alternative titles plus exactly the cited papers; causal gene withheld (idea.md 'Design rationale').

Entries: 100 drawn at random with a fixed seed, 20 per creation-era band of entry number; eligibility 2-12 references, causal gene in gene map, >=5 phenotype annotations, >=1 in-scope curator paragraph; sample is stratified and selects well-annotated, molecularly characterised entries (log Sec. 1.1).
Papers: 515 cited; readable in full 96 (19%), abstract only 345, title only 74; open access via PubMed Central or Europe PMC; supplementary material not retrieved (log Sec. 1.1).

Reference with required wording (notes.md 'Words to use'): 'OMIM facts conveyed' = coverage of facts in OMIM's allelic-variant descriptions as deposited in ClinVar, from OMIM's gene entries, variant-centred; 476 paragraphs in scope; split once into 6,652 fixed facts without sight of any draft. Narrative sections of phenotype entries are not compared.

Clinical synopsis reference = HPO disease annotations: 2,311, of which 1,835 are the HPO team's own curation from papers and 476 taken from OMIM; never call it OMIM's synopsis. Causal gene from OMIM gene map via MedGen and mim2gene; inheritance from HPO and MedGen as coarse classes; 427 in-scope OMIM-submitted ClinVar variants (log Sec. 1.1).
Other evaluation sets: 40-entry ablation subset, 30-entry replicate subset, 12 entries with 30-75 references (exploratory), 30 entries created June-November 2026 (log Sec. 1.1).

Model and settings: one model (Claude Opus 5.5) via the Claude Code command-line interface in headless mode with schema-constrained output; no temperature or seed exposed; reasoning effort high for writers, medium for per-paper extraction, audit and judging; no web access; replies cached so each call is made once (log Sec. 1.2).

content_bullets: Completion as an outcome (idea.md 'Formal setup'; log Sec. 1.4): a strategy completes an entry when its draft exists and no per-paper call failed; compare only on entries every compared strategy completed; sensitivity analysis counts a missing draft as zero. Rationale: one-call strategies lose the entry, per-paper strategies lose a paper (idea.md 'Design rationale').

Audit: atomic claims attributed to cited papers; verdict v(c, d) in {supported, partly supported, unsupported, contradicted} with a quote that must occur verbatim, else downgraded; claim verdict is the best over R(c); one repair round. Report 'judged supported' and keep unsupported and contradicted separate (notes.md).

Primary endpoint: coverage = (present + 1/2 partial) / facts judged over the fixed fact lists Phi(g); no fact went unjudged in any run (log Sec. 1.4). Explain why fixed lists: per-draft splitting adapts to the draft and changes denominators (idea.md; log Sec. 4.4).

Secondary: HPO precision/recall/F1 exact, hierarchical (ancestors count) and semantic; allelic variant recall and precision matched on normalised protein or nucleotide change with a model judge for names that do not normalise, not validated against reference sequences; causal gene F1; inheritance agreement as coarse classes; predicting nothing where the gold set is non-empty scores zero (log Sec. 1.4).

Statistics: paired differences from direct reading, bootstrap 95% interval over entries (10,000 resamples), median difference, exact sign test, Holm correction across secondary headline measures; primary endpoint not adjusted (log Sec. 1.4 and header).
All verdicts and fact judgements are by the same model that wrote the drafts; no human validation.

content_bullets: Completion first (log Sec. 2.1): 93 of 100 entries compared; per-strategy complete / incomplete / no draft (e.g. direct reading 97 complete, 3 no draft; evidence graph 96, 3 incomplete, 1 no draft); stopped replies remove entries unevenly.

Compact Table 2 from log Sec. 2.2/2.3: primary endpoint direct reading 49.1%, evidence graph 48.6% (-0.5, -1.5 to +0.5), agentic 48.4% (-0.6, -1.3 to -0.0), case table first 47.2% (-1.9, -3.1 to -0.7), memory only 15.1% (-34.0), recall then verify 14.6% (-34.5); plus claims judged supported, HPO exact F1, variants recovered, variant precision, gene F1, inheritance.

Interpretation bounded by log Sec. 4.2: differences of about one point or less over 93 entries are within replicate noise (half-width 1.0 point); so the agentic -0.6 and evidence-graph -0.5 are not distinguishable from noise. Do NOT claim the evidence graph conveys fewer facts overall; mention in one sentence that an earlier analysis treating completion unevenly showed -2.1 and the corrected analysis does not (log Sec. 12).
Sensitivity with missing drafts as zero (log Sec. 2.4): same picture (e.g. evidence graph -0.2, agentic +0.4, case table -1.4 (-4.1 to +1.4)).

Structured fields: extract-then-write raises synopsis recall but lowers precision (e.g. precision 40.6% graph vs 44.1% direct) and produces more variants not in OMIM (pooled precision 69.3% graph, 65.6% table vs 87.5% direct; log Sec. 2.6), noting precision counts a variant OMIM does not list as a miss whether or not the paper reports it.

Memory-based strategies: recall, then verify keeps claims judged supported high (94.2%) but conveys 14.6% of facts and states no inheritance in 22 of 93 entries (log Sec. 2.7); by construction it cannot add content from papers. Do not claim verification after recall cannot help in general.
Cost per entry at list price for one model (log Sec. 2.12): everything $1.18 direct reading vs $1.72 evidence graph, $1.78 case table first.

subsections.subsection_title: 4.2 Access to the source bounds agreement with curators
content_bullets: Lead with the within-paper hidden-full-text experiment (log Sec. 6.2; fig_hidden_fulltext): 49 entries, 91 hidden papers; on 46 entries / 136 paragraphs coverage 35.5% abstract only, 41.4% with second-hand passages, 78.6% with full text; state it uses the earlier per-draft fact splitting and that only the full-text draft had a repair round.

Where missed facts went (log Sec. 3; fig_missed_facts): of facts direct reading did not fully convey, 49% were in the text for full-text papers vs 2% for abstract-only and 0% title-only; overall 43% conveyed, 4% omitted though stated, 13% omitted and partly stated, 40% not in the available text. Model judgement.

Observational evidence (log Sec. 2.8, 2.9; fig_access_strata): pooled coverage 77.6% on full-text papers vs 40.1% abstract vs 17.5% title for direct reading; differences between strategies grow with the full-text share (case table first +0.6 / -4.0 / -6.1; agentic -0.1 / -0.4 / -2.0). Say explicitly this comparison is across papers and confounded with entry creation date and journal.

Report both halves of the claim (notes.md): at current open access the reading strategies are close; where more full text is readable, differences grow. Do not claim the method matters little in general.

Second-hand evidence in use (log Sec. 6.3, 96 entries): +1.8 points (+1.0 to +2.8) on the primary endpoint, +5.0 on variants recovered, title-only coverage 17.5% -> 26.7%; costs: unsupported before repair 0.4% -> 3.9%, facts contradicted +0.2 (+0.0 to +0.5); 240 of 10,597 claims rested only on second-hand text and were labelled, not counted as supported.

subsections.subsection_title: 4.3 What the audit can and cannot see
content_bullets: What it removes: memory-only control has 50.8% claims judged supported, 22.1% unsupported but only 0.6% contradicted before repair (log Sec. 2.2); pooled 576 unsupported vs 18 contradicted (log Sec. 2.5) - unsupported is not wrong (log Sec. 12). Reading strategies reach ~96% judged supported.

Planted errors (log Sec. 11): in 60 audited paragraphs one fact altered by rule; all 60 flagged on the altered claim; no unaltered controls, so false-flag rate unknown; omissions and misattributions not tested; 6 of 60 had other claims flagged too.

Blind spot from the hidden-full-text experiment (log Sec. 6.2): 112 claims rested on second-hand text; against the real full text 74 supported, 24 partial, 11 unsupported, 3 contradicted; table passages worse (9 of 21 unsupported) than paragraph passages (2 of 91). 'Unsupported by the primary text' is an upper bound because supplementary material is excluded.
The audit checks fidelity to the cited text, not correctness: a faithful copy of a source's error passes (log Sec. 12; notes.md).

Disagreements with the reference in at most one sentence as unconfirmed leads adjudicated by the same model (37 contradicted facts; paper judged to support the draft in 22; log Sec. 11), no entry named, no claim that OMIM is wrong.

By creation era (log Sec. 2.11; fig_memory_by_era): memory-only facts conveyed 14.5%, 24.1%, 17.5%, 12.6%, 5.7% from oldest to newest band, against direct reading 34.9-53.9%; memory gene F1 falls to 41.2% in the newest band.

Entries created June-November 2026 (log Sec. 10): 20 compared of 30; memory only 7.0% facts, gene F1 30.0%, claims judged supported 26.2%; reading strategies 49.4-52.2%; synopsis and inheritance not reported (annotations for one entry only). Model training cut-off is not known; stopped replies were frequent (agentic writer stopped on 6 of 30).

Hedge (notes.md): the control shows memory contributes little for the newest entries; within abstract-only papers, direct-reading coverage also declines with creation date (log Sec. 2.10: 49.8% for 600000-609999 to 37.9% for 620000 onward, 33.0% classic), so reading results are not claimed free of memorisation.

Setup (log Sec. 5): 40 entries weighted to full text (25 with at least half full text), 38 compared; 'matched' raises per-paper extraction to high effort and lets the writer choose synopsis terms (two changes made together); 'plus text' also gives the writer the papers' text.

Results: evidence graph matched vs direct reading +1.8 (+0.4 to +3.3) on facts, +3.3 (+1.2 to +5.6) on full-text papers; case table gap -2.3 shrinks to -0.2 when matched (table matched minus table +2.1, +1.1 to +3.2). Attribution of the matched gain to extraction effort is an inference (log Sec. 5).
Synopsis precision remains lower than direct reading for all extract-then-write variants (-2.6 to -5.7) and more terms per entry; plus text recovers claims judged supported (+1.5 graph).

Report the higher cost (generation $0.32 direct vs $0.65-$0.97) and completion losses from stopped high-effort extraction calls. Always phrase as 'our extract-then-write implementations' with the matched ablation beside the main-comparison result.

Learned guide (log Sec. 8): two reflection rounds on 27 training entries; the final guide did not improve facts on its own training entries (+0.06 points); on 68 held-out entries +1.0 (+0.0 to +2.0) facts, -1.6 variants recovered. Null-to-small result; says nothing about better-resourced prompt optimisation; a first guide that treated three empty drafts as omissions was discarded.

Reconciled case database (log Sec. 7): 57 merges proposed, 40 accepted in 27 entries; counted individuals 2,580 -> 2,413, families 1,126 -> 1,092; planted test merged 10 of 10 copied reports and no unrelated records (easy case only); no entry-level score changed (+0.1 facts, -0.1 to +0.4); patient-count agreement with HPO fractions 48% before and after. Not validated against external per-patient ground truth; do not claim structure pays when the database is the product.

Measurement stability (log Sec. 4.1-4.3), one short paragraph: judge re-runs within-entry SD 0.8-0.9 points, per-fact agreement 95.7%; three full replicates: within-entry SD 2.5 (direct) and 4.0 (graph), 1-3% of variance within entries; crediting a fact anywhere in the draft changes coverage by at most one point.

With model, sources, guards and scoring fixed, reading strategies differ by about two points or less on the primary endpoint at current open access, while access to full text moves coverage by tens of points within the same papers (log Sec. 2.3, 6.2).

Strategy differences grow where full text is readable (log Sec. 2.9, 5), so the comparison should be revisited as open access grows; this is a statement about this benchmark, not a general claim that strategy matters little.
An audit against the cited text is useful for removing unsupported claims but is a fidelity check: it cannot certify correctness and passes second-hand support (log Sec. 6.2, 11, 12).

Memory alone supplies little for recent entries; verify-after-recall as implemented cannot add content (log Sec. 2.11, 10, 12). Do not generalise the negative results for recall-then-verify, the learned guide or reconciliation beyond the implementations and entry sizes tested.
One model family wrote, audited and judged everything; no human has read any draft, verdict or fact judgement; no second model tested (log Sec. 12; notes.md).

The reference is indirect and narrow: variant-centred curator paragraphs, an HPO annotation set from two sources, gene and inheritance tables; narrative sections of entries are not compared; editorial agreement suggests drafts make about twice as many statements per paper as the paragraph has facts (log Sec. 8).
Oracle references: every strategy is given the curators' reference list; finding the literature was tested only on ten entries (log Sec. 11: 56 of 85 references, 66%).
Open access only, no supplementary material; variant names not validated against reference sequences; inheritance compared as coarse classes.
Strategies were developed on the same entries they are evaluated on; no separate development set.
Stopped replies remove entries unevenly across strategies (log Sec. 2.1, 10).

Entries with few references dominate; inputs too large for one prompt were not tested; the 30-75-reference tier (log Sec. 9) is exploratory: about ten comparable entries, mostly abstracts, fact score covers a minority of references.
Cost is at list price for one model; published systems were not run as released.

Restate the three questions of idea.md 'Problem' and answer each with the bounded claim from Sec. 4 (strategy: close at current access; access: within-paper drop 78.6% -> 35.5%; audit: fidelity, not correctness).

Position the benchmark and harness as the contribution (idea.md 'Contributions' 1): public sources only, claim-level audit, fixed fact lists, per-entry release of drafts, verdicts and scores (score files carry fact identifiers and statuses, not curator wording; notes.md 'Ethics').
No promises of further experiments (other models, curator studies, published systems).
Built from public resources (NCBI, ClinVar, HPO, MedGen, Europe PMC, HGNC); curator-written text used for scoring and not redistributed (notes.md 'Ethics and data use').
Generated entries are drafts for expert review, not clinical guidance, must be marked machine generated and not as OMIM content; rights holders' terms of use apply to anyone rebuilding the reference.
No human subjects; no patient-level data beyond what published papers report.
Model, interface and reasoning-effort settings; caching so each call is made once; no temperature or seed exposed (log Sec. 1.2).
Entry sampling with a fixed seed, eligibility rules and subsets (log Sec. 1.1); per-entry release of drafts, verdicts and scores; replicate and judge-variation analyses (log Sec. 4).
Total model usage: 37,769 cached model calls, 252 million input and 69 million output tokens, about $2,831 at list price (log Sec. 13). No repository URL or package name (anonymity).

Full log Sec. 2.2 tables (all metrics, volume per entry), Sec. 2.3 paired differences, Sec. 2.4 sensitivity with full statistics (median, sign test), Sec. 2.5 pooled counts, Sec. 2.6 variant precision, Sec. 2.7 inheritance errors by kind, Sec. 2.8 pooled coverage by access, Sec. 2.9 variant strata, Sec. 2.10 era-by-access tables, Sec. 2.12 cost.
State the earlier per-draft scoring row runs 2-5 points higher with the same ordering (log Sec. 4.4).
